newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV joins Sudan oil consortium.
newsitem.headline: OMV joins Sudan oil consortium.

text.p: Austria's OMV AG has taken a 27.5 percent stake in an international consortium that will drill for crude in Sudan, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.
The group, led by Canada's International Petroleum Corporation (IPC) and including Malaysian state oil company Petronas, will explore Sudan's Block 5A.

Under the terms of an agreement signed with the Sudanese government in February, state firm Sudapet has a five percent interest in the operation, leaving IPC with 40.375 percent, Petronas with 28.5 percent and OMV with 26.125 percent.
"With this project OMV intends to extend its exploration and production activities in an area with a great deal of hydrocarbon potential," OMV said.
The group would carry out a seismic study this year and had committed itself to two drills.
Block 5A is close to Blocks 1,2 and 4, which have proven oil reserves of 600 to 800 milion barrels, OMV said.
A planned 250,000 bpd pipeline from Blocks 1,2 and 4 to the Port of Sudan would have some 100,000 bpd in spare capacity for third parties, it added. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
